PRECAUTIONS
1. The solution should not be overheated while evaporating it.
2. The crystals should not be dried over the Bunsen burner.
3. All the glasswares should be handled with care.
4. Mother liquor should be rejected carefully so that there will be no
loss of crystals. Note: It is very difficult to obtain the absolutely pure crystals of the ingredients by fractional crystallization method.

Practical Chemistry
EXPERIMENT NO. 5
Object: TO RECOVER THE PRECIPITATE OF BARIUM SULPHATE
IN PURE AND DRY STATE
APPARATUS REQUIRED
Funnel Beaker Filter paper Test tubes Air oven Asbestos sheet Glass rod
CHEMICAL REQUIRED
1. Silver nitrate solution
2. Barium chloride solution
3. Sulphuric acid solution
THEORY

Barium sulphate (BaS04) can be obtained in solid state by treating barium chloride solution with excess of sulphuric acid solution. This is precipitation reaction that can be defined as the double decomposition reaction in which an insoluble solid is formed by the action of two substances in solutions. The insoluble solid formed is called precipitate.
Here, BaS04 is formed as a white precipitate which can be obtained in pure state after several washings.

BaC12 (aq) + H2S04 (aq) ----..-..-.--...--...+ BaS04 (s) + 2HC1 (aq) white ppt The purity of the precipitate can be checked by treating the pptwashed water with few drops of AgN03 solution and BaC12 solution separately. Presence of chloride and sulphate ions is indicated by formation of a white precipitate respectively with these two reagents.
AgN03 (aq) + Cl- (aq) AgCl (s) + No; (aq) white ppt BaC12 (aq) + SOZ- (aq) BaS04 (s) + 2C1- (aq) white ppt
Separation of Mixtures
PROCESS
Liquid Filter paper Filtrate Figure 2.6: Filtration Take a half test tubeful of barium chloride solution in a beaker.
Add dropwise nearly less than a half test tubeful of dilute sulphuric acid of equal molarity. After each addition, stir the solution with a glass rod.
A white precipitate will be formed. Heat the solution to boiling and allow it to stand to enable the precipitate settle down.
Take few ml of the supernatant liquid (clear liquid above the ppt) in a test tube and add 2 drops of the precipitant (i.e. H2S04 solution) .
If a white ppt appears, add few more drops of the precipitant to the solution in the beaker.
Heat the solution to boiling, allow it to stand to settle down the ppt and check the completeness of precipitation as in number (4).
If the fresh ppt appears in the test tube, the precipitation is incomplete. Add few more drops of dilute H2S04. The completion of precipitation reaction should be checked again.
Practical Chemistry If no fresh ppt appears in the test tube, the precipitation is complete.
After this, heat the solution to boiling. Allow it to stand for some time. Decant off the supernatant liquid.
Wash the precipitate with distilled water three to four times by the process of washing by decantation.
Take the precipitate-washed water in two test tubes. Add few drops of AgN03 and BaC12 solutions separately.

Formation of a white precipitate with AgN03 solution indicates the presence of chloride ion (either BaC12 solution or HCl solution) in BaS04 ppt. Similarly, formation of a white precipitate with BaC12 solution indicates the presence of sulphate ion (H2S04 solution) in BaS04 ppt.
